items.title: Uber beats Waymo as first to launch robotaxis in London
items.topic: Uber beats Waymo as first to launch robotaxis in London
items.summary: Uber has launched its robotaxi service in London, becoming the first company to do so in the city. This deployment marks a significant milestone in the expansion of autonomous vehicle services in Europe, potentially challenging established players like Waymo.

items.topic: Waymo Robotaxi Rides Are Now Open To The Public In Denver, San Diego And Tampa
items.summary: Waymo has expanded its robotaxi service to the public in Denver, San Diego, and Tampa, bringing the total number of cities with Waymo robotaxis to 14. items.title: Enhancement of Large Language Models Driving Knowledge for Practical Autonomous Driving Decision Making
items.topic: Enhancement of Large Language Models Driving Knowledge for Practical Autonomous Driving Decision Making
items.summary: The IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology published a study on enhancing large language models (LLMs) for practical autonomous driving decision-making. The paper introduces a question-guided multimodal graph-based retrieval-augmented generation (QGM-GRAG) approach to improve LLMs' theoretical driving knowledge and hazard perception, crucial for safety-critical tasks. This research addresses the gap in current LLMs' driving theory capabilities and assesses its impact on driving decision-making and safety.

items.title: Real-Time Vision-Language Model Guided Semantic-Aware Diffusion Navigation with Intelligent Vehicle Validation
items.topic: Real-Time Vision-Language Model Guided Semantic-Aware Diffusion Navigation with Intelligent Vehicle Validation
items.source: 2025 IEEE 28th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITSC)
items.summary: The 2025 IEEE 28th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITSC) featured a paper on a vision-language model guided semantic-aware diffusion navigation method (VLSAN) for semi-structured campus road scenarios. VLSAN translates natural language instructions into vehicle motion control by generating semantically guided drivable region maps, achieving multimodal information fusion and semantic alignment. This method enhances natural interactive navigation in autonomous driving systems.

items.title: A Collaborative Multi-Modality Interaction for VLA-based End-to-End Autonomous Driving
items.topic: A Collaborative Multi-Modality Interaction for VLA-based End-to-End Autonomous Driving
items.summary: A paper in arXiv proposes a robust Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model for end-to-end autonomous driving that combines multi-modality interaction with multi-trajectory planning and optimization. This system addresses the limitations of existing VLA models, which often formulate driving as a visual question-answering task, leading to unreliable and less interpretable decision-making. The proposed framework aims to improve reliable and interpretable driving reasoning in complex scenarios.
